minutes.headline: Sewer Commission voted to waive interest for one prompt-paying customer and others who come forward, over billing-mail problems.
minutes.summary: The commission discussed a costly engineering quote for a pump-station energy study needed for a grant, manhole repair scoping and whether Chapter 90 could pay part of it, and a turnover procedure for cash. Most of the evening went on interest waivers for bills many customers say they never received, which ended in a split roll-call vote. It also agreed its position on an overdue liquor-license account ahead of the Select Board hearing.

what_happened.line: The commission voted to waive interest for one contested customer and any customer who was current and comes forward within seven days; the roll call was split.
It declined the engineering firm's energy-study task order for pump stations; the business manager will seek the information elsewhere before the May 10 grant deadline.
On manhole repairs, a member will ask the state aid engineer whether Chapter 90 can cover covers and frames, and Bill will ask about hiring a contractor to inspect and price repairs.
The commission took no vote on an overdue liquor-license account; it will tell the Select Board the account must be paid in full by the deadline or the license should not be renewed.
The Q4 bill insert wording was accepted by consensus without a vote.

why_it_matters: Sewer customers who say they never received a bill, and were current, may have interest waived if they come forward within seven days of the vote.
Billing-software problems kept demands from going out in two quarters, which cost the sewer enterprise fund revenue and bears on receipts and on future sewer charges.
Manhole repair costs could exceed the budgeted amount, and whether Chapter 90 money can help is still open.
watch_next: May 10 grant deadline for the pump-station energy study; no application will be filed if the information cannot be obtained.
Next commission meeting: the procurement officer's answer on a manhole inspection contractor, and the Select Board hearing on the liquor-license account.
